title: OC Nathaniel Hackett Press Conference | Week 10 vs. Los Angeles Rams
headline: Rookie QB Carson starts Sunday behind a possible sixth different O-line combination, and Reggie Virgil and Simi Fehoko are named as receivers who must step up.
summary: Hackett spent most of the session praising the rookie quarterback, Carson, who is set to start Sunday. He called him a fast processor who is confident, studies constantly, and has the experience of an older rookie. Hackett said the biggest jump to the NFL is the post-snap speed and the even matchups, which force weekly changes to the play calls. He said the offensive line may be another new starting combination, the sixth this season, and he stressed next-man-up and the linemen working in unison. He called protecting against the opposing pass-rush front, led by Myles Garrett, a major challenge. He pointed to the defense's ability to rush the passer and drop into coverage from the interior. On Carson's accuracy, he said it comes from quieter feet and growing comfort in the system, not from mechanics or arm strength. On the receivers, he called Reggie Virgil explosive downfield and Simi Fehoko dependable, citing a key out-route catch against Dallas. He said many different pass catchers will be put in position to help Carson. He wants Carson to play freely, with off-platform creativity but not many no-look throws yet.

signals.claim: Virgil is expected to be one of the receivers asked to step up and make plays downfield with the rookie QB starting.
signals.note: He is billed as the explosive downfield option, so he could see deep targets if he gets a bigger role.
signals.quote: Reggie obviously he's explosive. He does some great things down the field.

signals.claim: Fehoko is a reliable receiver who will be used as the rookie QB's dependable target.
signals.note: He is seen as a trusted, steady option, which may help his floor with a first-time starter at QB, but nothing points to a volume jump.
signals.quote: He's always doing the right thing.

topics.detail: Carson, a rookie, is set to start Sunday. Hackett praised his processing, preparation and confidence, and said his accuracy is improving as his feet quiet down and he grows comfortable with the concepts. Carson is not on the supplied roster, so he is not listed in the signals.

The group could be a sixth different starting combination this season. Hackett stressed next-man-up and working in unison. The injury report lists Hjalte Froholdt, Jon Gaines and Isaac Seumalo as DNP, but Hackett did not address them.

Hackett called the opposing front, led by Myles Garrett, very good and said Garrett moving inside creates problems. The plan is to mix creative looks with core concepts, and he expects a major challenge.
Hackett wants a prepared, confident QB who plays freely. Off-platform plays are welcome, but he does not want many no-look throws yet.

title: Tommy Rees, Jeff Ulbrich, & Craig Aukerman on Falcons preparation for Chiefs | Press Conference
headline: Rees says the offense is "close" but inconsistent; Corey Levin steps in at center for Ryan Neuzil, Penix is scrambling more, and Pitts' volume is still a want rather than a promise.
summary: This was a joint session with the defensive and special teams coordinators, and Rees's portion starts around the Corey Levin question at 21:00. Rees said the team is expected to move forward at center with Levin, who knows Coach Callahan's run and communication schemes. He praised Ryan Neuzil but declined to say which center is the better scheme fit. He said Levin's extra weight could make the interior pocket a bit more stout and change some run-game combinations. He credited Michael Penix Jr. for three scrambles for about 50 yards against Cincinnati, saying quarterbacks who pick up a couple of first downs a game with their legs help top third-down offenses. Rees put the blame for the offense falling short on himself and the staff, citing penalties, mental errors and calls he wanted back. He said that cost the team points last week, and he mentioned several drives that either stalled or came away empty. He highlighted Bijan Robinson's rail-route explosive and his edge speed at the goal line, and he praised Drake London's blocking as the best he's seen from a receiver. On Kyle Pitts, he said two explosive plays (about 40 yards) were wiped out by penalties and that he wants the volume up, without promising it. He also covered attacking pressure with quick throws, screens and run-game shots, and called the Chiefs' defense under Spagnuolo versatile, aggressive and third in total defense.

signals.claim: Levin will start at center and run the offensive line communication going forward.
signals.note: A stable, experienced center who knows the run schemes helps the run game and Penix's protection, which supports Bijan and the passing offense.
signals.quote: we expect Corey to play at a high level for us

signals.note: Rees spoke of Neuzil's contributions in the past tense and focused on Levin as the starter, so Neuzil appears to be out of the center role, though the transcript doesn't explain why.
signals.quote: everything he did for us and did for this organization for a lot of years

signals.claim: Penix will keep using his legs to pick up first downs on scrambles.
signals.note: Scramble yardage gives Penix a rushing floor and helps keep drives alive on third down.
signals.quote: I thought Mike did a great job being vertical in the pocket

signals.claim: Bijan will keep creating explosive plays in both the run game and the passing game, including on rail routes.
signals.note: Rees pointed to Bijan's edge speed near the goal line and his explosive rail route as drive-starters, which supports his touchdown and big-play upside.
signals.quote: He's fast. Yeah, he is fast.

signals.claim: The staff wants to increase Pitts' target volume, but Rees did not commit to it.
signals.note: Two explosive plays to Pitts were called back by penalties last week, so his production looks lower than his usage, but the volume is not guaranteed to rise.
signals.quote: Do we want his volume to be up. Yeah.

signals.claim: London will keep being used as an elite blocker and as a screen target on the perimeter.
signals.note: His blocking sets the tone and helps the run game, and perimeter screens to him are one way Rees attacks pressure, so his role goes beyond catches.
signals.quote: I would be hard pressed to find a better blocking receiver in the NFL, period.

topics.detail: Rees said the offense is close but that close isn't enough. He blamed penalties, mental errors and calls he wanted back, saying that is the difference between scoring 17 and scoring 35. He wants more explosives in both the run and the pass and said they left points on the field last week.

Rees said quick throws, screens and run plays can become explosives against blitzes because defenders have fewer bodies in space. He pointed to the Chicago two-minute drill as an example and said everyone must be on the same page for it to work.
Rees called Steve Spagnuolo's unit versatile and aggressive, third in total defense and consistently one of the league's best. He said it will be a great test.

The defensive coordinator discussed life without Jessie Bates III and the team's struggling run defense. The special teams coordinator said the kicker Nick was replaced and the team is bringing in Jake Moody, who practiced well.

title: Declan Doyle Discusses Jacoby Brissett, Pre-Snap Penalties
headline: Jacoby Brissett starts at QB for Baltimore this week. Doyle expects a more vertical, under-center offense, which should help Derrick Henry, while Mark Andrews' drops remain a concern.
summary: Doyle said Jacoby Brissett, whom Baltimore just acquired, is starting at quarterback this week. He called the position the biggest factor in winning and said Brissett is picking up the offense quickly and bringing stability. There is no carryover or shared history with him yet, so installs go back to basics. Doyle admitted the team is new to each other and has to accelerate to get on the same page. He defended his play-calling in the earlier Joe Fagnano stretch, including the empty-formation call to Zay Flowers at the 7-yard line, and praised Fagnano as a warrior. He is excited about Brissett's ability to stretch the field vertically, and the plan is to tailor the game plan to what Brissett is comfortable with. Doyle called the pre-snap penalties incredibly frustrating. The team has revisited cadence, motion and timing, and the new quarterback's different cadence gives them a chance to reset. On Mark Andrews, he acknowledged the drops but pointed to his contested third-down catches and said everyone on offense has to pick it up. He said Brissett's vertical threat and under-center work should lighten boxes for Derrick Henry.

signals.claim: Brissett starts at QB this week and the offense will throw downfield more than it did with Fagnano.
signals.note: A veteran starter who plays on time and can stretch the field gives the passing game a steadier, more vertical look than the recent backup-led stretch.
signals.quote: he plays on time, he plays within rhythm. He has great feet.

signals.claim: Brissett's under-center and vertical passing should mean fewer loaded boxes for Henry.
signals.note: A more credible downfield passing threat should give Henry more room to run.
Doyle acknowledged Andrews' drops and said everyone's numbers are down, offering no promise of a bigger role. He did praise the contested third-down catches.
signals.quote: We love the way he works.

signals.note: Fagnano was praised for handling a tough spot, but Brissett's arrival pushes him back to the backup role.
signals.quote: he's a warrior.

topics.detail: Baltimore leads the league in pre-snap penalties, and Doyle called it incredibly frustrating. The team has reviewed its cadence, motion and timing, and used the new QB's different cadence as a reset, starting Wednesday with clap drills and cadence work.

Brissett has no history in this offense, so installs are a first for him and the team is going back to the building blocks. Offensive staffers Izzy and Marcus Brady have worked with him before, which helps.
Doyle said he tailors the plan to the quarterback's comfort through constant dialog. He won't call plays Brissett doesn't believe in.

Doyle defended the play-calling after Fagnano entered: a double-move shot to Josh Cuevas, then an empty-formation call at the 7-yard line that ended in a sack. The next game's plan leaned on Derrick Henry and short passes for run-after-catch.

title: Pete Carmichael On The Bills Run Game, Navigating Injuries, And Facing The Jets
headline: James Cook handled a 31-carry workload against Minnesota and remains the centerpiece of the run game, while Tylan Grable is stepping in on an injury-thinned offensive line.
summary: Carmichael said the Vikings game was always going to be a hard-fought four-quarter game, so Buffalo stayed committed to the run. He praised James Cook for handling 31 carries, noting that early two- and three-yard gains grew into chunks of four to seven yards. He said that whenever the ball is in Cook's hands he feels good about the outcome. He also praised Joe Brady's growth as a head coach, calling him detailed, positive, and the same person every day. Tylan Grable has been getting more opportunities as a fill-in lineman. Carmichael said he fits in quickly with the group and keeps improving with more reps. He called a third tackle who can play both sides a huge asset. He credited the offensive line coaches and the unit's next-man-up approach after a stretch of players in and out of the lineup. Looking ahead, he described the Jets as an attacking, disruptive, fast defense, said Buffalo has its work cut out, and singled out edge rusher David Bailey as someone you have to account for on every snap.

signals.claim: Cook remains the focal point of the ground game and can handle a heavy workload like the 31 carries against Minnesota.
signals.note: A coordinator who trusts Cook to carry 31 times and wants the ball in his hands supports a high-volume outlook, especially in game scripts where Buffalo leans on the run.
signals.quote: any time you have the opportunity to put the ball in his hands

signals.claim: Grable will keep getting offensive line snaps as a versatile swing tackle who has played both right and left tackle.
signals.note: He is filling in on a banged-up line (Spencer Brown and Dion Dawkins are both limited), so his continued play affects pass protection and run blocking for Cook and Josh Allen.
signals.quote: he just continues to just get better as more and more chances he gets.

topics.detail: Buffalo expected a physical four-quarter game against Minnesota and committed to the run. Carmichael said persistence paid off as short gains turned into bigger ones.
Carmichael praised the line's next-man-up mentality, tight-knit communication, and the two offensive line coaches' work with so many players in and out. He did not name specific injuries.

Carmichael said Brady has grown since their time together in New Orleans, with more detailed command of the run game, pass game, and protections. His personality is unchanged: positive, energetic, and clear in communication.

He called the Jets an attacking, disruptive defense with speed at every position group. He said edge rusher David Bailey is a big part of what they do and that Buffalo must know where he is at all times.

title: Coordinators Press Conference | Week 10 vs. New Orleans Saints
headline: Xavier Legette is nearing a return as a deep threat but must earn his snaps behind a productive receiver and tight end group; Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble stay central, and Bryce Young is playing healthy without the knee brace.
summary: Brad Idzik said the Panthers are 'in the driver's seat' in the division and that the room has reset after a three-game losing streak by focusing on the details and returning to the run game, explosive plays and finishing games. He explained the goal-line sequencing behind Sunday's intercepted pass to Tommy Tremble: the team wanted balance so the defense couldn't pin its ears back, and he said he trusts his gut and the numbers. He praised the tight ends for their physicality and versatility, saying Tommy Tremble's run-game aggression opens seam and flat routes, and Darren Waller plays like a receiver while 13 personnel forces defenses to honor the run. On Xavier Legette, whose practice window has just opened, he said the easiest way to bring him back is to run him vertically, but he must earn reps because Metchie, David Moore and the tight ends have been producing. He said Bryce Young's lack of a knee brace gives him a more 'free flow' game, though the brace wasn't the reason for lower rushing totals. Trevor Etienne got praise for decisive, downhill runs and kick returns despite limited live reps. Idzik spoke warmly about Jonathon Brooks' leadership while he works back from another surgery, and about Monroe Freeling's steadiness as a first-round rookie tackle facing top pass rushers. The special teams and defensive coordinators also spoke, but their comments are summarized under topics.

injuries.detail: Hurt on a deep post in Atlanta; his practice window just opened and he is easing back, with Idzik planning to use him vertically but making him earn reps.
Played last week without the knee brace and isn't on this week's report; Idzik said it's nice for him to shed it mentally and physically.
Coming back from another surgery and still in a return-to-play timeline; Idzik said he isn't physically on the field yet, though the injury report lists him as a full practice participant (groin).
Defensive coordinator Todd Wash said he and other injured defenders are out practicing, but declined to say anything about their game status.

signals.claim: Will be reintegrated primarily as a vertical deep threat and will have to earn his snap share rather than get an immediate full workload.
signals.note: Expect a gradual return with a deep-ball role while Metchie, Moore and the tight ends keep their production-based snaps.
signals.quote: get him running and stressing the defense vertically

signals.claim: Will keep his receiver role because he has been producing while Legette was out.
signals.note: Idzik cited Metchie among the producers Legette must earn reps against, so his role looks safe even as Legette returns.
signals.quote: whether it's Metchie or Beaty or David Moore in spots

signals.claim: Will continue to be used as a receiver-style weapon, including out of 13 personnel.
signals.note: He leads the team in catches and touchdowns, and Idzik sees him as a mismatch that forces defenses to choose between nickel and honoring the run.
signals.quote: Darren Waller just being the big special athlete that he is

signals.claim: Will keep getting seam and flat targets as defenders overplay his run-game aggression.
signals.note: He has three touchdowns this season and Idzik explicitly credits his run-blocking for opening receiving chances.
signals.quote: he gets to slip them and get open on seam routes or flats

signals.claim: Young is healthy and playing without the knee brace, and the offense wants to tap into his play-extending ability.
signals.note: Healthier mobility should help his scrambling and third-down plays, supporting both his passing and rushing upside.
signals.quote: there's a free flow nature to his game that we always want to tap into

signals.claim: Will remain a limited-carry backup who is ready to contribute whenever his number is called.
signals.note: Idzik is pleased with his decisive downhill running, but he is not getting the bulk of the early carries.
signals.quote: That's the guy we want to see.

signals.note: Idzik praised his work ethic but gave no timeline, so he is not a usable fantasy piece yet.
signals.quote: He's not the loudest guy, but he's always working.

signals.note: The first-round rookie is steadily improving against strong pass rushers, which matters for Young's protection.
signals.quote: he's adding tools to his tool belt every week

topics.detail: Idzik defended the pass play to Tremble that was intercepted inside the five, saying the team wants balance so defenses can't pin their ears back to stop the run. He relies on probability numbers and his gut on game day, and said he loses sleep over sequencing.
Idzik said the offense is resetting each week after a three-game losing streak and wants to return to the run game, the pass game and explosive plays.
Idzik said the loud New Orleans dome requires a silent cadence, but he sees the atmosphere as energizing rather than negative.

Anthony Tyus III has been praised as a primary returner who runs hard and also covers kicks. Punter Sam Martin is slightly ahead of last year's pace, and kicker Ryan's misses have all come to the right, a technique issue the staff is working on. Trevis Gipson is campaigning to return kickoffs.

Wash is calling plays in his first game as DC, with an attacking front. He said Lee Hunter played only 13 snaps because of a miscommunication and will play more, and said Turk is a good fit for the attack style. He also said the secondary is working to cut down on illegal-contact penalties.

title: Travis Switzer Press Conference : November 12th, 2026
headline: Deshaun Watson returns at QB vs. Houston's elite pass rush, Quinshon Judkins' downhill running is praised, and the staff wants Harold Fannin Jr. involved earlier.
summary: Switzer said his expectations for Deshaun Watson on his return haven't changed: sound operation, protect the ball, make the expected plays and let it rip. The staff reviewed their slow starts and found they have already tried early runs, movement passes and other approaches, with nothing standing out, so they will keep stressing fast starts in practice. Penalties are a major focus, especially pre-snap and snap-count errors, which he called the least tolerable. The staff is also frustrated by failing to close out games with a four-minute offense. Houston's pass rush shapes the entire pass game plan through chips, route distribution, quick throws and protection answers. He praised Quinshon Judkins as a physical, downhill, hard-to-tackle runner who gets yardage when there isn't much there. He also said run efficiency, such as turning 2-3 yard gains into 4-6, matters more than explosive runs. On the red zone and goal line, he said the offense must be better against movement and execute better on the fourth-and-one. He added that Harold Fannin Jr. and other top skill players should get touches early, and that they aren't opposed to direct-snap or Wildcat looks.

injuries.detail: The reporter framed this as Watson's return this week; Switzer discussed expectations for him and gave no injury details.

signals.claim: Watson returns to the quarterback role this week with the same expectations as before.
signals.note: Watson's return changes the offense's QB situation, but Switzer gave no specific plans and only repeated basic expectations (take care of the ball, make the plays).

signals.claim: The staff will keep using chips and game-plan help against elite edge rushers, including Houston's, while Fano keeps developing his technique.
signals.note: Fano has struggled against strong edge rushers lately and faces another tough pass rush, so sack and pressure risk for the offense stays elevated.
signals.quote: he's shown the ability to be as good as he wants to be

signals.claim: Judkins will remain the main downhill runner, with the staff working on other run schemes with him.
signals.note: Switzer's praise for Judkins' physicality and efficiency supports a steady rushing workload.
signals.quote: very physical, um, downhill runner and he's tough to tackle

signals.claim: The staff will try to get Fannin touches early in games, and direct-snap looks with him are not ruled out.
signals.note: The staff wants to get him the ball early, which supports his target and touch volume, though his groin injury is a concern.
signals.quote: always getting our best skill players touches um throughout any part of the game

topics.detail: The staff reviewed early-game play calling and found no standout fix, having tried runs, movement passes and other plays. They will emphasize fast starts in Wednesday's tempo period.

Penalties are a key problem. The offense will focus on pre-snap and snap-count penalties and on closing out games with a four-minute offense. Head coach Monken showed the team penalty stats in a meeting.

Switzer said a good red zone offense starts with running the ball. The goal-line failures against New Orleans stemmed from movement by the defense and timing and execution on the fourth-and-one, not a lack of push.

He values moving the line of scrimmage and efficient runs over explosive ones. Run-game success depends on numbers, angles and matchups, much of it through tight ends, and the staff has seen growth up front.
The staff scouts opponents' tendencies, sometimes going back years, and calls plays that target the best players and are familiar to the quarterback.

title: Klayton Adams: Press Conference | Week 10 vs. 49ers | 2026
headline: Cowboys are thin at RB and TE, and Klayton Adams says Javonte Williams' heavy workload needs managing against the 49ers. Expect creative personnel groupings and a still-unnamed No. 2 back.
summary: Adams opened by saying the Cowboys are thin at running back and tight end. He said they will build personnel groupings around who can do the job on a given play and how the defense responds. Extra tight ends or receivers can force base or sub defenses, and he stressed that nobody cares about injuries. He said Broderick Jones' role as an extra tackle or jumbo tight end simplifies the defensive looks the team has to plan for. Jones is also being prepared for more meaningful snaps later. He praised Ryan Flournoy's mentality and importance after the catch that set up the game-winning touchdown. He said CeeDee Lamb is hard to defend because he can line up anywhere and do the dirty work in the run game. On Tyler Booker, he said the scheme is getting easier and he is anticipating more, though he is not all the way there yet. On Javonte Williams, he agreed the consecutive 20-carry games are a concern and that the second running back matters more. He admitted the team still has to figure out who the next man up is. He praised the 49ers' attack front and Fred Warner, and said motion and formation variety make the defense harder to read. He also said he re-checks his tendencies on this defense each week because it has changed subtly from last year.

injuries.detail: Did not practice with a knee issue per the injury report. Adams referred only to depth issues at tight end and did not name him.
Did not practice with an ankle issue per the injury report. Adams referred only to depth issues at running back and did not name him.
Limited with a hamstring issue. A reporter noted he missed the previous game.

signals.claim: The Cowboys will try to limit Williams' workload and give a second running back a larger role, but that back has not been identified.
signals.note: Williams' volume is high but could be trimmed, and a currently unnamed back could gain value if the team follows through.
signals.quote: Short answer yes and yes.

signals.claim: Jones will keep playing as an extra tackle or jumbo tight end and is expected to get more reps as the season goes on.
signals.note: He is a blocking-role player, but his growing snaps could slightly cut into other tight ends' snaps in heavy sets.
signals.quote: He's done a nice job for us in the role that he's been playing

signals.claim: Flournoy is valued as an important offensive piece beyond his stats.
signals.note: He has trust from the coaching staff, but his role is described as unglamorous and may not produce consistent fantasy numbers.
signals.quote: he just he means a ton to us

signals.claim: Lamb will keep lining up inside, outside and in run-game roles, which makes him hard to take away.
signals.note: His versatility keeps his target floor high even when defenses focus on him.
signals.quote: it makes him really hard to defend

signals.claim: Booker is anticipating plays better and the scheme is getting easier for him.
signals.note: A more comfortable guard helps the run game and pass protection, which supports Williams and the passing offense.
signals.quote: The scheme part is becoming easier for him.

topics.detail: Adams said the team will use extra tight ends or receivers to get the defensive look it wants. The focus is on whether a player can do the job on a given play.

Adams called the 49ers' attack front built to stop outside zone and said they draft to that philosophy. Fred Warner's pre-snap adjustments let the other defenders play freely, and the unit has stayed strong against the run despite injuries on the line.
Adams said varied formations and motion make it harder for veterans like Warner to key on tendencies. He downplayed any special recommitment to motion, saying each week's plan differs.
The Cowboys signed a practice squad player named Miller, whom Adams described as having good size and quickness. A coach had him in New Orleans and the terminology is similar.
Adams re-checks his long-term tendencies on the 49ers each week. He said this defense differs subtly from last year's, so he avoids planning for things they no longer do.

title: Petzing on offensive urgency
headline: Petzing shrugs off Goff's new injury-report listing ('No concerns'), says Gibbs' receiving dip is game-script driven, and says Mahogany returns to the line vs. the Patriots.
summary: Petzing blamed the red-zone slump on self-inflicted problems: penalties, a couple of missed pre-snap identifications, and drives that put the offense behind the sticks. He also noted that two kneel-downs in the last three games drag the numbers down. His main theme was urgency from the first snap. He said the offense has finished the last three games running the ball with more edge than it showed early, and he wants that attitude on every play. Miles Frazier was praised for his fill-in work, but Christian Mahogany is expected back at guard on Sunday, and Petzing was confident he will bounce back from last week's violation. Juice Scruggs has impressed at center in place of Cade Mays, and Petzing called a healthy Mays's return a 'good problem'. Petzing said the lower receiving numbers for Gibbs come from coverage, scheme, a 57-play game and late-game runs rather than a deliberate choice. He also said he wants to find more chances for Isaac TeSlaa, and he praised Amon-Ra St. Brown, DeAndre Carter and TeSlaa's blocking. On Goff's new injury-report listing he said only 'No concerns.' He closed by saying he only cares about scoring one more point than the opponent, despite the offense staying under 20 points since the Cardinals game.

injuries.detail: Listed as limited with a chest issue. Petzing had 'no concerns' when asked about it.
Has been out with an ankle injury (did not practice), and Juice Scruggs has been playing center. Petzing gave no return timeline and only referred to the situation for when Mays is healthy.
Expected to step back into the lineup Sunday after last week's violation. Petzing said he can get back on the horse without missing a beat.

signals.claim: Mahogany returns to the starting offensive line vs. the Patriots on Sunday.
signals.note: A stable starting line helps protection and the run game, and Petzing praised his 100 mph play.
signals.quote: Absolutely.

signals.claim: Frazier goes back to a reserve role when Mahogany returns Sunday.
signals.note: He played well as a fill-in, but he is not expected to keep a starting spot.
signals.quote: assignment wise, communication wise and effort wise was excellent

signals.claim: Scruggs remains the center while Mays is out, and may compete with Mays for the job once Mays is healthy.
signals.note: Goff trusts him, and the center spot could be a real competition when Mays returns.
signals.quote: I think Jared has a ton of trust in him and a ton of faith.

signals.note: Petzing called his consistency nearly historic and says it is the same every game, so he remains the offense's most reliable piece despite the limited-practice rib listing.
signals.quote: It's every single day. It's every single play.

signals.claim: The offense will look for more targets and opportunities for TeSlaa in coming games.
signals.note: He has only two catches in four games, but the coordinator trusts him in key situations, so a few more targets are possible.
signals.quote: we have to try to find you some opportunities here and there.

signals.claim: Carter will be used in the game at any moment in a rotational role.
signals.note: He has earned trust fast and is a dynamic ball carrier, but the usage described is rotational rather than a heavy role.
signals.quote: He learns the playbook really quickly.

signals.claim: Gibbs' receiving production dipped because of coverage, scheme, low play volume and late-game run calls, not a deliberate de-emphasis.
signals.note: His catch total could bounce back if games are tight or the team is trailing late and the offense passes more.
signals.quote: sometimes it's scheme or coverage that they're playing

signals.claim: Goff's chest issue is not a concern for Sunday.
signals.note: He appeared on the injury report as limited, but Petzing signaled no worry.
signals.quote: No concerns.

topics.detail: Petzing blamed penalties, missed pre-snap identifications and getting behind the sticks. He also said two kneel-downs in the last three games skewed the numbers.

He wants first-snap intensity and said the offense has had more attitude late in games than early. He said it needs to be present in practice and walkthroughs, and that there is no easing into an NFL game.
He said New England's deep-pass damage vs. Green Bay came largely on contested throws and catches. The offense needs to win one-on-ones in protection and at the catch point.
Offense has been under 20 points since the Cardinals game but is still winning. Petzing says he only cares about scoring one more point than the opponent.

title: Houston Texans Coordinators addressed the media
headline: Tank Dell has no restrictions and can play all three WR spots, while David Montgomery's return is still unclear and Caley stayed vague on the RB split.
summary: Offensive coordinator Nick Caley (the transcript also includes the special teams and defensive coordinators, whose remarks are left out here) said the Texans will go to Cleveland with weather contingency plans on the call sheet and won't be thrown by the forecast. He called the Browns one of the fastest and most aggressive defenses in the NFL, with a disruptive, athletic interior. He said he tries not to lean on stats, such as Cleveland's poor run defense or Houston's weak run game, and instead builds a run menu around matchups and the feel of the game. On Tank Dell, he said there are no restrictions, he can play all three receiver spots, and last week's positive yardage and staying on schedule let the offense keep moving. On the backfield, he was noncommittal: David Montgomery is working back, and Emari Demercado had a first-down run, but Caley spoke only about managing reps and formatting roles through the week. He praised C.J. Stroud for his consistency, poise and distribution of the ball, and said trust in protection and timing explains the quarterback's jump in aggressive throws. A young lineman's first NFL action was also discussed, but the transcript doesn't make clear who is meant.

injuries.detail: Did not practice with a groin issue per the injury report. The question described him as working his way back, but Caley gave no timeline and spoke only about monitoring reps.
Listed as limited with a hand injury. Caley said there are no restrictions and he will be ready to go when called.

signals.claim: Will play without restrictions this week and can line up at all three receiver spots.
signals.note: A full-go, versatile Dell in a spread-the-ball offense supports a steady or growing snap share against Cleveland.
signals.quote: He'll be ready to go.

signals.note: He sat out practice with a groin issue and Caley offered no clear timeline, so his availability and workload depend on how the week's practices go.
signals.quote: being conscientious of monitoring reps.

signals.note: He was named in the RB question, but Caley only said roles are being formatted through the week, so his share of carries depends on Montgomery's status.

signals.claim: The offense will keep pushing the ball downfield because of trust in protection and timing.
signals.note: Stroud is sixth in aggressive throw percentage, and Caley credits trust and a second year in the system. He also called him elite at spreading the ball around, which supports the whole receiver group.
signals.quote: We all have so much trust and confidence in him.

topics.detail: Caley said the staff always has weather contingency plans on the call sheet. Extreme wind could change the passing approach and lean toward concepts friendlier to the quarterback and receivers.

Caley avoids leaning on stats such as Cleveland's poor run defense or Houston's weak run game. The plan is built around early-down and situational run menus plus the flow of the game, like last week's rhythm, which mixed in 11 personnel.
He called the Browns one of the fastest and most aggressive defenses in the NFL, with a disruptive interior that gets off the ball quickly and plays hard.
A young lineman who could see his first NFL action was praised as smart and sharp and for moving around positionally, but the player isn't clear from the captions.
Caley said the system has been strengthened by a year of debriefing and ownership from players and staff. He credited Stroud's consistency, poise and hunger.

title: Campanile & Udinski on Prep for Divisional Matchup with Titans | Press Conference
headline: Udinski says Bhayshul Tuten is carrying the backfield load while playing through injury, and the Jaguars want a more explosive run game against Tennessee.
summary: The transcript is a joint session. The first part is defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile on the midseason defensive trades and the Titans' offense. Udinski's answers start around the Walker Little question. He called Walker Little a true starter who has grown at guard, right tackle and left tackle, and he credited rookie guard Emmanuel Pregnon for his growth despite some penalties and assignment errors. He used Parker Washington's 50-yard touchdown and a tight-window throw to praise the trust and film-study work between Trevor Lawrence and his receivers. Tuten did not practice last week but played on the short week and handled 12 touches and a touchdown. Udinski called that selfless and tough, and noted he might not be 100%. He called rookie Josh Cameron a versatile weapon who lines up at tight end, back, slot and outside. He also said Jakobi Meyers is very effective finding voids in the middle of the field, though the credit goes to all 11 players. Udinski wants the run game more efficient and explosive after a week he said fell short of the team's standard. He said Tennessee, now without Jeffery Simmons, will force contingency plans because of shifting defensive alignments.

injuries.detail: Did not practice last week but played on the short week, with 12 touches and a TD. Udinski said he may not be 100% and is doing extra work in the training room. The injury report lists him as DNP with an ankle injury this week, and the coach gave no update for Sunday.

signals.claim: Walker Little is the starting left tackle and is playing with confidence.
signals.note: A settled, improving offensive line helps the run game and Trevor Lawrence's pass protection.
signals.quote: he's continued to work like he is a starter and he is a starter

signals.claim: Pregnon will keep playing as a rookie starter while the staff works on his penalties and consistency.
signals.note: The physical tools are showing, but penalties and assignment errors are still a concern for run-blocking consistency.
signals.quote: he attacks those errors and his areas of improvement just about as hard as anybody

signals.claim: Washington has earned Lawrence's trust on option routes and can produce explosive plays.
signals.note: His 50-yard touchdown showed a growing rapport with Lawrence that supports a bigger role.
signals.quote: there's certainly an element of trust with that

signals.claim: Lawrence is playing with confidence and making tight-window throws that let the offense scheme varied routes.
signals.note: The coordinator is describing a quarterback with command of the offense, which is good for the whole passing game.
signals.quote: embodies the conviction and the confidence that Trevor is playing with

signals.claim: Tuten remains the lead back carrying the load.
signals.note: He handled 12 touches and a touchdown on a short week, which suggests a heavy workload if healthy.
signals.quote: he's been carrying the load for us

signals.claim: Tuten may continue to play through the injury without being 100%.
signals.note: He is on the injury report as DNP with an ankle injury, so his practice participation this week matters for lineup decisions.
signals.quote: when he might not be 100%

signals.claim: Cameron will keep lining up at tight end, back, slot and outside receiver.
signals.note: A multi-position role gives him several paths to touches, though the usage is hard to predict.
signals.quote: the physical ability to be almost playing like a tight end sometimes

signals.claim: Meyers will keep being a primary target on middle-of-the-field routes.
signals.note: He is a reliable target for Lawrence over the middle, but he is on the injury report with an ankle injury (DNP), so his availability needs watching.
signals.quote: a phenomenal job finding those voids in the middle of the field

topics.detail: Udinski wants the run game more efficient and explosive than last week and below the team's standard. The plan is to get backs in space and favorable matchups while staying ahead of the sticks.
Tennessee plays its second game without Jeffery Simmons, who lined up all over the line. The Jaguars have contingency plans for players aligning differently and will adjust in game.

Campanile was excited about the three midseason defensive additions, including interior linemen, and said they are learning the verbiage quickly. Brian Thomas Jr.'s name does not appear in his remarks.

title: Eric Bieniemy on Falcons: 'Defensivly They're Doing an Outstanding Job' | Press Conference 11/12
headline: Bieniemy praised Kelce as the team's receiving-yards leader and said new WR Josh Downs is being eased in with Sunday possible; Mahomes took a hit before halftime but didn't miss a snap.
summary: Bieniemy opened by saying the offense started slow in the win, then picked it up in the second half. Most of the questions were about the late first-half play where Patrick Mahomes was hit. He called it a communication and awareness lapse in pass protection, put it on the right tackle and on Emmett Johnson to read the situation and help, and said he wasn't blaming Emmett. He said Mahomes got up and didn't miss a snap. He called new receiver Josh Downs a sharp, high-character player who is blending in well. The staff is being careful not to overload him as it gets him ready to potentially play Sunday. He spoke warmly about Travis Kelce, who leads the team in receiving yards in year 14, crediting his will to win, leadership and preparation. He deflected a question about IR tackle Josh Simmons to Reid and the training staff. He called the Falcons' defense sound, fast and aggressive, praised coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, and said the team can't overlook them despite their record.

injuries.detail: Was hit just before halftime but stayed in the game without missing a snap; he was a full practice participant with an elbow listing.
On IR; Bieniemy deflected questions about his rehab and meeting attendance to Reid and the training staff.

signals.claim: Kelce remains the team's leading receiver and a central part of the offense.
signals.note: Bieniemy sees Kelce's production as sustainable and tied to his work habits, which supports his continued target share.
signals.quote: I'm not shocked that he's leading us.

signals.claim: Mahomes took a hit before halftime and did not miss a snap.
signals.note: No sign of a lingering issue from the hit, but the pass-protection breakdown is worth monitoring.
signals.quote: for him to get up, to get back out there and not miss a snap

signals.note: He was involved in the pass-protection lapse that led to the Mahomes hit; Bieniemy didn't blame him but stressed he needs a better feel for the situation.
signals.quote: Emmett just has to have a feel and do his part.

topics.detail: Bieniemy said the offense needs better awareness and accountability, with linemen and backs giving chip help when a matchup is bad. He called the Mahomes hit a valuable lesson, not a scheme error.

The new receiver is being brought along carefully, with Sunday possible. Bieniemy called him sharp, said he has a good feel for the game, and said he is blending in well. Downs is not on the provided roster.
Bieniemy called Atlanta fast, physical and sound, and praised coordinator Jeff Ulbrich. He noted Jessie Bates was traded and said the Falcons' record doesn't matter.

title: Andrew Janocko on the Raiders offense: ‘We’re a collective of preparation’
headline: Fernando Mendoza starts at QB for the Raiders vs. Seattle; Janocko downplayed any special rushing role and gave no backfield or target news.
summary: Janocko spent the session on rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza taking over as starter from Kirk Cousins ahead of a game at Seattle, where the Raiders face Mike McDonald's defense. He declined to promise a bigger designed-run element, saying legs come into play for every quarterback and that if Mendoza's skill set offers an edge, "you might see" it. He framed readiness as the whole offense's collective preparation rather than a single moment for Mendoza, and cited Mendoza's growth in mastering the offense and explaining it to teammates. On the matchup, he called Seattle's defense well coached, world class and a tough test for a rookie QB, and said the Raiders will try to replicate game-like looks but mostly focus on executing and trusting their training. He had warm words for Cousins, calling his impact on the building process tremendous, and acknowledged his own emotions about facing his former organization before saying the focus is on the job. No injuries, depth chart changes, or specifics on running backs, tight ends or receivers were given. Tyler and Jalen were mentioned only as examples of players held to the same competitive standard.

signals.claim: Mendoza will start at quarterback against Seattle, and his legs may show up in the game plan to some degree.
signals.note: Mendoza's mobility could add a modest rushing element to his fantasy profile, but Janocko did not commit to it and played it down.

signals.claim: Seattle's defense will be a major challenge for the rookie, and the Raiders will try to simulate game-like looks in practice.
signals.note: A tough road matchup against a well-coached defense that tends to blitz rookies more is a risk for Mendoza and the offense's output.
signals.quote: it's about going out, trusting your training and sticking to your techniques.

topics.detail: Janocko praised Kirk Cousins as a leader, person and friend, and said his impact on the team's build will last, but he kept the focus on the next game.

Janocko, a former Seattle assistant, said emotions run high this week because of his ties there, but he is setting them aside. He called Seattle's defense well coached and said the Raiders will focus on their own execution.
He stressed collective preparation and competition on every rep, treating Mendoza as one of 11 players held to the same standard rather than a special case.

title: OC Bobby Slowik - Nov 12 | Press Conference
headline: Kyle McCord starts at QB vs. the Colts with Malik Willis on IR for about 4-5 weeks. Expect fewer QB runs and more rhythm passing, and center Aaron Brewer is in concussion protocol.
summary: Slowik called the second-quarter drive against Detroit miserable. A holding penalty wiped out what he saw as the biggest play of the game, and further penalties and a sack kept the offense behind the chains. He said the penalties had been cleaned up since the bye, then "crept up and reemerged" against the Lions. His coaching point was that a foul ends the play, so players need to play clean. With Malik Willis headed to IR for roughly four to five weeks, Kyle McCord will make his first real NFL start. Slowik said the offense won't change much, but there will be fewer plays built around the QB running. He praised how quickly McCord has picked up the system after arriving without any camp reps. He also pointed to McCord's college experience as a help with nerves, and said McCord has been excellent in practice. If Aaron Brewer can't clear concussion protocol, Andrew Meyer would step in at center with little scheme change, and he has already been taking snaps with McCord. If Chris Bell can't play, Slowik said Jalen Tolbert is reliable and versatile, which matters with a young QB. He also praised the receiver room generally, including the three rookies, Jared Wayne and the practice-squad players.

injuries.detail: Placed on IR after laboring through the Detroit game. Slowik expects him out about four to five weeks.
In concussion protocol and did not practice. Slowik discussed Andrew Meyer as the replacement if Brewer can't play.
Limited in practice with a knee issue. The question described his status as uncertain, and Slowik talked through Tolbert as a fill-in.
Slowik referred to the team having lost him earlier in the year and adjusting the run game. No current status was given.

signals.claim: McCord will start at QB against the Colts, with a full week of first-team reps.
signals.note: He is the starting QB while Willis is on IR, so he is a streaming option in a pass-first, rhythm-based offense with no QB-rushing upside.
signals.quote: he's he's been knocking it out of the park in practice

signals.claim: Willis will miss about four to five weeks on IR.
signals.note: He is out of lineups for the stretch, and the offense loses his rushing production at QB.
signals.quote: four weeks, five weeks, whatever it is

signals.claim: Brewer may miss Sunday because of concussion protocol, with Andrew Meyer stepping in at center.
signals.note: His status affects the offensive line and a first-time starter at QB, so check the final injury report.
signals.quote: if it winds up being Meyer, like we'd be excited for his opportunity

signals.claim: Meyer will start at center if Brewer can't play, with no scheme changes.
signals.note: He has practiced with McCord, so the center-QB exchange should be smooth and the offense shouldn't be disrupted.
signals.quote: him and Kyle have been getting all the snaps together

signals.claim: Tolbert could see more receiver snaps if Chris Bell can't play, though Slowik did not commit to it.
signals.note: He is a veteran who can line up at multiple spots, and Slowik wants reliable players around McCord, so he is a deep-league watch if Bell is out.
signals.quote: He can play multiple spots.

topics.detail: Slowik said the offense had cleaned up penalties since the bye, but they resurfaced against Detroit, including a holding call that wiped out a big play. This week's emphasis is playing clean football and staying on schedule.

Play calling won't change much. Slowik said McCord can run the pass and run concepts, but there will be fewer plays that rely on the QB running. He described the offense as rhythm-based, with throws out on time.
Slowik referred to the earlier loss of De'Von Achane and the adjustment the run game made then. His point was that the staff believes everyone on the roster can run the offense.

title: Josh McDaniels 11/12: "We got a lot of guys that we have confidence in"
headline: With Rhamondre Stevenson out for a stretch and TreVeyon Henderson out with illness, Corey Kiner looks set to lead the Patriots backfield against Detroit in Germany.
summary: McDaniels said losing Rhamondre Stevenson for a stretch hurts because he is such a valuable part of the offense. He said the team has had many players taking reps all year and trusts the running backs to fill in, while being careful not to give them more than they can handle. He singled out Corey Kiner, who has been with the team only 8-9 weeks, as a young player making steady progress in every area and said he has a lot of confidence in him for Sunday. On the offensive line, he talked about constant shuffling, especially at guard. He said the team is not unique in dealing with injuries and will go into the game with what it feels most confident doing. He said the heavy shuffling also limits how much tempo or no-huddle the offense can run, so the focus is clean football and taking care of the ball. On Drake Maye's turnovers, he blamed a tipped ball and a split-second error against good Detroit safeties, and called ball security an ongoing goal. He described Detroit's defense as playing very well over the last month, with more than one good pass rusher and young linemen taking on bigger roles. He mentioned Hutchinson and McNeil (named in the captions as Hudson and McNeil).

injuries.detail: McDaniels said he is "going down for a little bit" and the team will feel the loss. He did not give a timeline. He did not practice (DNP, knee) on the injury report.
Listed out with illness on the injury report. McDaniels did not clearly address him by name in the transcript.

McDaniels said he is excited to see a player back on the practice field and called it a boost, but the captions never make clear who he meant. The injured linemen on the report are Walter Rouse, Greg Van Roten and Morgan Moses.

signals.claim: Stevenson will miss time, and other running backs will absorb his role.
signals.note: Losing the lead back removes his volume and shifts carries to the backups.
signals.quote: you feel it because he's such a valuable part of everything you do

signals.claim: Kiner will take on a bigger running back role against Detroit on Sunday, handling both rushing and pass-catching work.
signals.note: With Stevenson and Henderson both out, Kiner is the likely lead back, but McDaniels hinted at limiting the role to what the young backs can handle.
signals.quote: we've seen solid progress from him in every area

signals.claim: Ball security remains a team focus and goal, and Maye's turnovers will stay under scrutiny.
signals.note: McDaniels blamed a tipped ball and a late read against strong Detroit safeties, so turnover risk persists in a tough matchup.
signals.quote: games where we don't turn the ball over

topics.detail: The team has used many guard combinations because of injuries. McDaniels said this affects what the offense can do each week, and the game plan will lean on what the group does best.

McDaniels said the summer talk of playing fast was meant to improve communication and ownership, not to become a no-huddle team. Changing line combinations make it harder, so the emphasis is on clean plays and taking care of the ball.
McDaniels called Detroit a very good unit over the last month. He pointed to pass rushers Hutchinson and McNeil, young linemen taking on bigger roles, and strong safeties who punish mistakes.
McDaniels said playing in Germany changes the atmosphere and the team is not feeling extra pressure. Players get extra time together on the trip.

title: Doug Nussmeier on Audric Estimé, Cesar Ruiz | Saints vs. Panthers 2026 NFL Week 10
headline: Estimé's big, north-south running was praised after the Browns game, Jordyn Tyson's snaps were deliberately managed in his first game, and Cesar Ruiz starts at center this week.
summary: Nussmeier credited the run game's success against the Browns to physicality. He praised the offensive line, the backs hitting holes, and the receivers blocking on the perimeter. He said the opening-play double-team combination blocks were an existing play, not a new invention. He called William Sherman's work as a jumbo tight end effective because it created gap-fit problems for the defense. That package was something the staff identified over the bye week. Cesar Ruiz will start at center this week. Nussmeier called him a natural center who was worked there in camp as a contingency plan, and said the move was well thought out, though shifting two linemen is always a dilemma. Jeremiah Wright is part of the interior shuffle. He played in the Paris game against Pittsburgh, is still on a learning curve, and Nussmeier said he's excited to see him play. Nussmeier described Jordyn Tyson's debut as a mix of good things and items to clean up. His snaps were kept in a controlled range, and the staff got some production. He treated Tyson's fumble on his first catch near the goal line as a teachable moment. He singled out Audric Estimé as a big, thick, north-south runner who suits the physical approach and the "dirty three" yards.

injuries.detail: He did not practice Thursday (biceps) per the injury report. Nussmeier did not mention him or give a reason for Ruiz moving to center.

signals.claim: Estimé's physical, between-the-tackles style fits the run game's current emphasis and should keep him involved.
signals.note: The coordinator singled out his downhill running as a fit for the physical run identity, which supports a continued carry share.
signals.quote: big thick runner. He's going to take the ball and go north and south.

signals.claim: Tyson's snaps were deliberately held in a controlled range in his first game and may grow as he learns.
signals.note: Production came on limited, managed snaps. A fumble on his first catch near the goal line was framed as a teachable moment, not a demotion.
signals.quote: I thought we were able to keep his snaps in the right range

signals.claim: Ruiz will start at center this week against Carolina.
signals.note: An offensive line shuffle affects run-blocking cohesion, which matters for the backs.
signals.quote: it's the right decision. And I'm looking forward to watching Caesar play there.

signals.claim: Wright will play on the offensive line this week as part of the interior shuffle around Ruiz.
signals.note: He is a young lineman with a learning curve, so the interior line is a mild risk for the run game.
signals.quote: excited to see him play this weekend.

signals.claim: Sherman will keep being used in the jumbo tight end role that the staff identified over the bye week.
signals.note: The package adds a heavy run-game look, with little direct fantasy value for Sherman himself.
signals.quote: having the ability to use Sherm the ways we were able to

topics.detail: Nussmeier said the run game got going against the Browns because the team's energy and physicality beat theirs. He credited the line, the backs hitting holes, and receivers blocking physically on the perimeter. He said perimeter blocking has been a long-running emphasis and showed up well on tape.
The double-team combination blocks and insert on the first play were an existing play, not a new invention. The goal is to cover up defenders and get the back started.
Ruiz moves to center, which the staff prepared in camp as a contingency. Nussmeier acknowledged that changing two spots at once is always a dilemma.

title: OC Frank Reich Press Conference (11/12) | Week 10
headline: Reich says Breece Hall and Braelon Allen are co-'1A' backs, with about 90% of the split left to in-game feel, so don't expect a clear lead back vs. Buffalo.
summary: Reich framed the week around a tough matchup with the division-leading Bills, praising their pass rush and the 'big trade' for Hooker. His offensive plan is to be efficient and explosive, balance run and pass, take shots, and run the ball to neutralize a good defense. He said facing a high-scoring opponent mostly changes fourth-down aggressiveness, which Aaron Glenn sets in advance each week and which helps Reich's play-calling. On the red-zone struggles, he argued defenses don't change coverage until roughly the 15-yard line, so the whole playbook is open until about the plus-30. The fix, he said, is better coaching, calling, sequencing and execution. He explained the four second-half run calls as a repeat of the previous week: three-and-outs on third down let the other offense get hot, and he said he only passed when he might have run on one or two calls. On the backfield, he called Hall and Allen '1A' players, said about 10% of calls designate a specific back, and said the rest are left to the position coach's feel for the flow of the game. He rejected the idea that players are pressing mentally and downplayed a sideline flare-up from last week as a non-issue.

signals.claim: Hall will keep sharing backfield work with Braelon Allen, with only about 10% of plays pre-designated for a specific back.
signals.note: There is no clear lead back and the red-zone touches are determined by game flow, so Hall's touch volume and goal-line work are hard to project.
signals.quote: obviously we got two one A players

signals.claim: Allen will keep sharing backfield work with Breece Hall, with in-game feel from the RB coach deciding most red-zone usage.
signals.note: Reich treats him as an equal to Hall rather than a backup, which gives Allen real flex or handcuff value, but his role stays unpredictable.
signals.quote: obviously we got two one A players

topics.detail: Reich called Buffalo a very good team and defense with strong edge rushers (including Rousseau and Chubb) and said the new addition Hooker is a great player. The plan is to be efficient and explosive, mix run and pass, and take shots.

Against a high-scoring opponent like Buffalo, Reich said the fourth-down charts change. Glenn tells the staff how aggressive to be each week, which lets Reich call earlier downs knowing whether they'll go for it.

Reich said defenses don't change coverage until about the 15-yard line and the full playbook is available until roughly the plus-30. He called the red-zone struggles a coaching, sequencing and execution problem, not a scheme limit.

topics.topic: Second-half run game and third downs
topics.detail: The team ran only four times in the second half for the second straight week. Reich blamed three-and-outs and failed third-down conversions, which cut possessions and forced the Jets to play from behind, and said he only had a play or two he could have run more.
Reich rejected the idea that players are pressing in the red zone and shrugged off a flare-up involving the starting QB or right tackle as a normal heated moment, not a pattern.

title: Brian Daboll Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Daboll praised Cam Ward's steady growth, but Carnell Tate (shoulder, DNP) and Peter Skoronski (hamstring, DNP) look shaky going into a tough Jaguars run defense.
summary: Daboll said the offense clicked against the Bengals because of better execution, explosive plays in both the run and pass games, and better work in the red zone. He called tempo a situational tool: it was used heavily in the last two games to get Cam Ward into rhythm, and it comes and goes with the game plan. He said the deep passing game is built on a vertical element in almost every concept, and that contested catches and ball placement are worked on every day. Ward was described as improving each week at progressions, operation, protections, rhythm and sack volume, though Daboll admitted the results haven't shown in the win column. Daboll said the tight ends were sent out more last week, which gave Gunnar Helm more receiving chances, but tight ends are still asked to help in protection depending on the opponent's pass rush. He called Tony Pollard dependable and valuable, and said the Titans face possibly the league's best run-stop defense in Jacksonville. He respects the three players Jacksonville added at the deadline. On the line, he said the play calling barely changed when Peter Skoronski and JC Latham left the Bengals game, and he praised the backups.

injuries.detail: Missed the Cincinnati game and is listed as DNP with a shoulder issue this week. Daboll gave no update on his availability.
Left the Bengals game in the second half and was a DNP with a hamstring issue. Daboll gave no timeline and said he would love to have him back.
Also left the Bengals game in the second half, but he was a full participant this week (finger). Daboll gave no update on him.

signals.claim: Tempo will be used in some games to help Ward's rhythm, and Ward's protection and operation work will be tested heavily against Jacksonville.
signals.note: Ward is trending up as a young QB, and the offense uses tempo and quick reads to help him, but the protection challenge and sack volume are still concerns.
signals.quote: he's continually improved

signals.claim: Helm's receiving role depends on the game plan and whether tight ends are needed to help block.
signals.note: He had more chances last week when the tight ends went out as receivers, but his targets will vary with protection needs.
signals.quote: We had a lot more four out or five out.

signals.claim: Pollard remains a valued piece of the offense but faces one of the league's best run defenses in Jacksonville.
signals.note: Daboll praised Pollard's reliability and explosive handoff, but the Jaguars' run defense makes the matchup a tough one.
signals.quote: if not the best run stop defense in the league

signals.note: Tate missed the Cincinnati game and is a DNP this week, so his availability is unclear. His absence shifted receiver snaps to other players.

signals.claim: The Titans will rely on backup linemen if Skoronski can't play.
signals.note: The left side of Ward's protection is in question, and Daboll said the line's backups would step in with confidence.
signals.quote: confidence in the guys behind him

topics.detail: Daboll said the Titans went tempo-heavy in the last two games to get into rhythm, but it varies week to week. It can simplify things for a young QB by giving him more time at the line, depending on what the defense shows.

Almost every pass play has a vertical element, apart from three-step concepts. He said contested catches and throw placement are worked on at the start of practice each day and that the staff isn't seeing a pattern in the uncatchable deep balls.

A receiver whose name the captions garble stepped in for Tate at Cincinnati, played more snaps than he had all season combined, and produced. It is unclear whether Daboll meant Chimere Dike or Xavier Restrepo, so he is left out of the signals. Daboll said the player knows all the receiver spots and will be worked in more.

Daboll said he respects the three players Jacksonville added at the trade deadline, singling out safety Bates as an instinctive ball hawk and a big interior defensive lineman. Jacksonville's run defense is among the league's best, and protection and operation will be a big challenge.
